text:
Philip Broberg has taken over a much bigger job in St. Louis. He's playing 24:37 a night, up from 23:21, and he's on the ice for 54% of the team's power-play chances after 28% last season. With that role has come 17 points in 23 games, 0.74 a game against 0.42 a year ago. He's also at the very top of the league in top skating speed (24.3 mph).

Some of this is a real breakout. His own chances are up to 0.40 expected goals per 60 from 0.24, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him getting to the home-plate area more than 95% of defensemen last season. Some of it isn't. He's shooting 13% where our range says a true rate nearer 7%, and the Blues have scored 12.4 more goals than expected with him on the ice.

The thing we'd watch is five-on-five: St. Louis gets only 46.7% of the expected goals when he's out there, worse than without him. Our projection still has him between 41 and 60 points.
